title: Durian: A Web Vulnerability Scanner
description: A modular Python scanner for authorized web assessments, covering discovery, common vulnerability checks, session handling, and report generation.

sections.title: What I Built
content: The scanner is organized as a CLI-driven toolkit with separate crawler, session, scanner, model, and reporting components. This structure keeps discovery and assessment logic modular instead of coupling everything to one command.
The repository covers SQL injection, reflected XSS, path traversal, sensitive-file discovery, session handling, and report generation for controlled testing environments.

sections.title: How it works
content: Durian is a command-line scanner. It crawls the target to find links and forms, runs its scanner modules against what it found, and writes the results to a report. Cookies and authentication live in one session layer, so the crawl and every check run as the same user.

figure.alt: Diagram: a target URL goes to the crawler, which finds links and forms. The scanner modules test for SQL injection, reflected XSS, path traversal and sensitive files. The results go into a report. Session and authentication handling underlies the whole run.
figure.caption: The scan pipeline, from target URL to report.

bullets: The scan command runs every module against a target, and a modules option picks specific checks such as sqli, xss and traversal.
The crawl command maps a site's endpoints before anything is tested.
SQL injection checks are error-based and boolean-based, and the XSS checks look for reflected input.
The report command writes the findings to a file in a structured format.

sections.title: Security Value
content: The project demonstrates how I translate manual web-testing workflows into repeatable tooling while keeping scope, authorization, and reporting in mind.
On the roadmap: fixture applications, reproducible test cases, clearer severity logic, and sanitized output examples that show how findings become useful remediation work.
